outcome: catheter-related bloodstream infection (CRBSI) related to peripherally inserted central venous catheter (PICC)
cohort: The study included 680 neonates who received a peripherally inserted central catheter (PICC) in a neonatal intensive care unit between June 2020 and June 2023.
finding: Low birth weight, premature delivery, parenteral nutrition, long catheterization time, and 5-minute APGAR score <=7 are independent risk factors for catheter-related bloodstream infection in neonates with PICCs, with fungi and multidrug-resistant bacteria being the predominant pathogens.
